metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Unionville in Butler County? We buy Marcellus interests directly, explain your deed honestly, and pay cash.
heroLead: Butler County doesn't get talked about as much as Washington or Greene County when people discuss Marcellus drilling, but families around Unionville have their own long, complicated history with oil and gas that goes back further than most people realize.
intro: Unionville is a small unincorporated community in Butler County, north of Pittsburgh, in a part of the state that saw its own oil boom back in the 1870s and 1880s, long before anyone had heard the word Marcellus. That older history means a lot of Butler County deeds carry legacy oil and gas reservations layered underneath more recent Marcellus-era leases, and figuring out which set of terms actually governs your interest today takes careful review.

Butler County sits toward the edge of the Marcellus wet-gas window, with the play transitioning toward drier gas as you move north through the county, and Utica shale potential adding another layer of interest for some operators evaluating deeper rights here.

sections.heading: A County With Two Different Oil and Gas Eras
paragraphs: If your family's mineral rights near Unionville trace back to the late 1800s oil boom, you may be looking at an old shallow lease alongside a much newer Marcellus lease covering the same land at a different depth. These can coexist, and untangling exactly what each one covers is part of confirming what you actually have to sell.

sections.heading: What We Check Before Making an Offer
paragraphs: We review your full deed history, confirm whether your parcel sits inside any current Marcellus or Utica unit, and check for older shallow-well leases that may still be active. From there we give you a clear cash offer, explained honestly.

faqs.question: My family's oil rights near Unionville go back to the 1800s. Does that lease still matter?
faqs.answer: It might, if a shallow well tied to that lease is still producing or the lease otherwise remains in force. We review the specific history to confirm its current status.

faqs.question: Is Unionville in the wet-gas or dry-gas part of the Marcellus?
faqs.answer: Butler County sits near the transition zone. We check current geologic and unit data for your specific parcel rather than generalizing across the whole county.

faqs.question: Does Utica shale potential affect the value of my interest?
faqs.answer: It can add interest for some operators evaluating deeper rights, though Utica development in this area is less established than the Marcellus. We factor in realistic development likelihood rather than speculation.

faqs.question: What documents help speed up the review of an old Unionville-area interest?
faqs.answer: A copy of your deed is the best starting point. Old lease agreements, prior royalty statements, or probate paperwork also help, though we can typically locate what's missing at the Butler County recorder of deeds.
